"""llama.cpp backend for the installable agent: one ``llama-server`` process per deployment, serving a single
verified GGUF file over its OpenAI-compatible API.

Differences from Ollama that callers should know:

* Model files come from Hugging Face (pinned commit + SHA-256), not a model registry, and are verified before
  the server starts. ``start`` only allocates the instance; ``prepare_model`` downloads and launches.
* Only the OpenAI-compatible routes (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions) are exposed; Ollama-native /api/*
  routes are not available for llama.cpp deployments.
* CPU by default. GPU offload (-ngl) is used only for GPU deployments on a llama-server build that supports it.

Same isolation as the Ollama process backend: loopback port, own process group, minimal environment, and a
systemd user scope with hard memory/CPU limits when available. Not a security sandbox.
"""

import asyncio
import os
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

from .base import ProgressCallback, RuntimeCapabilities, WorkloadError, WorkloadHandle, WorkloadRuntime, WorkloadSpec
from .model_store import DEFAULT_ALLOWED_HOSTS, ModelStore, validate_source
from .process_utils import CgroupProbe, base_env, free_port, own_process, spawn, terminate

READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300


class LlamaCppProcessRuntime(WorkloadRuntime):
    name = "llamacpp"
    backend = "process"

    def __init__(
        self,
        data_dir: Path,
        binary: str = "llama-server",
        cgroup_limits: bool = True,
        allowed_hosts: tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_ALLOWED_HOSTS,
        store: ModelStore | None = None,
    ):
        self.data_dir = data_dir
        self.logs_dir = data_dir / "logs"
        self.binary = shutil.which(binary) or binary
        self.cgroups = CgroupProbe(cgroup_limits)
        self.store = store or ModelStore(data_dir / "gguf", allowed_hosts)
        self._procs: dict[str, asyncio.subprocess.Process] = {}

    async def capabilities(self) -> RuntimeCapabilities:
        version, available, detail = "", False, ""
        if os.path.isfile(self.binary) and os.access(self.binary, os.X_OK):
            proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
                self.binary, "--version", stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT
            )
            out, _ = await proc.communicate()
            text = out.decode(errors="ignore")
            for line in text.splitlines():
                if line.lower().startswith("version"):
                    version = line.split(":", 1)[-1].strip().split()[0][:50]
            available = proc.returncode == 0
            if not available:
                detail = "llama-server did not run"
        else:
            detail = "llama-server binary not found"
        cg = await self.cgroups.available()
        return RuntimeCapabilities(
            name=self.name,
            version=version,
            backend="process",
            available=available,
            gpu=False,
            limits_enforced=cg,
            detail=detail or ("cgroup limits via systemd user scope" if cg else "limits advisory"),
        )

    async def start(self, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> WorkloadHandle:
        validate_source(spec.source, needs_file=True)
        port = free_port()
        return WorkloadHandle(
            deployment_id=spec.deployment_id,
            base_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}",
            backend="process",
            ref={"port": port, "runtime": self.name},
        )

    def _argv(self, model_path: Path, port: int, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> list[str]:
        argv = [
            self.binary,
            "-m",
            str(model_path),
            "--host",
            "127.0.0.1",
            "--port",
            str(port),
            "-c",
            str(spec.num_ctx),
            "-t",
            str(spec.cpu_cores),
            "--parallel",
            "1",
            "--alias",
            spec.model_tag,
            "-ngl",
            "999" if spec.gpu else "0",
        ]
        return argv

    async def prepare_model(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec, progress: ProgressCallback) -> None:
        source = validate_source(spec.source, needs_file=True)
        free_mb = shutil.disk_usage(self.data_dir if self.data_dir.exists() else self.data_dir.parent).free // 2**20
        needed_mb = source.get("size", 0) // 2**20
        if not self.store.is_cached(source) and free_mb < needed_mb:
            raise WorkloadError("INSUFFICIENT_DISK", f"{needed_mb} MB needed for the model, {free_mb} MB free")
        model_path = await self.store.fetch_gguf(source, progress)
        await progress("Model verified (SHA-256); starting llama-server")

        port = handle.ref["port"]
        cgroup = await self.cgroups.available()
        self.logs_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
        proc = await spawn(
            self._argv(model_path, port, spec),
            env=base_env(self.data_dir / "home", spec.gpu),
            log_path=self.logs_dir / f"{spec.deployment_id}.log",
            scope=f"agentmesh-wl-{spec.deployment_id[:8]}-{port}" if cgroup else None,
            ram_mb=spec.ram_mb,
            cpu_cores=spec.cpu_cores,
        )
        self._procs[spec.deployment_id] = proc
        handle.ref.update({"pid": proc.pid, "cgroup": cgroup, "model_path": str(model_path)})
        await self._wait_loaded(handle, proc)

    async def _wait_loaded(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, proc: asyncio.subprocess.Process) -> None:
        """llama-server answers /health with 503 while loading and 200 once the model is in memory."""
        deadline = time.monotonic() + READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as client:
            while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                if proc.returncode is not None:
                    raise WorkloadError("RUNTIME_START_FAILED", "llama-server exited while loading the model")
                try:
                    if (await client.get(f"{handle.base_url}/health")).status_code == 200:
                        return
                except httpx.HTTPError:
                    pass
                await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        raise WorkloadError("RUNTIME_START_FAILED", "llama-server did not finish loading the model in time")

    async def verify_ready(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> str | None:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120.0) as client:
            try:
                resp = await client.post(
                    f"{handle.base_url}/v1/chat/completions",
                    json={
                        "model": spec.model_tag,
                        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK."}],
                        "max_tokens": 2,
                        "stream": False,
                    },
                )
            except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
                raise WorkloadError("HEALTHCHECK_FAILED", f"Test generation failed: {type(exc).__name__}") from None
        if resp.status_code != 200 or not resp.json().get("choices"):
            raise WorkloadError("HEALTHCHECK_FAILED", f"Test generation returned HTTP {resp.status_code}")
        return f"sha256:{spec.source['sha256']}" if spec.source else None

    async def health(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> bool:
        if not await self.is_alive(handle):
            return False
        try:
            async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as client:
                return (await client.get(f"{handle.base_url}/health")).status_code == 200
        except httpx.HTTPError:
            return False

    def _own_process(self, handle: WorkloadHandle):
        return own_process(handle.ref.get("pid"), "llama-server", handle.ref.get("port"))

    async def is_alive(self, handle: WorkloadHandle) -> bool:
        return self._own_process(handle) is not None

    async def remove(self, handle: WorkloadHandle) -> None:
        await terminate(self._own_process(handle), self._procs.pop(handle.deployment_id, None))

"""Model artifacts downloaded from an allowlisted source (Hugging Face) and verified before use.

Security properties:

* Only https URLs on allowlisted hosts are fetched, including every redirect hop, so a malicious catalog
  entry or control plane cannot make the worker request internal addresses (no SSRF).
* Repository ids, file names, and revisions are validated; revisions must be pinned 40-hex commits.
* GGUF files are verified against the catalog's SHA-256 and size before any runtime loads them, and are
  stored content-addressed (``<sha256>.gguf``) so a cached file cannot be swapped silently.
* Gated or private models are refused: no access tokens are sent to provider machines.
"""

import hashlib
import os
import re
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlparse

import httpx

from .base import WorkloadError

DEFAULT_ALLOWED_HOSTS = ("huggingface.co", "*.huggingface.co", "*.hf.co")
REPO_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,95}/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,95}$")
FILE_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,200}\.gguf$")
REVISION_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")
SHA256_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")
MAX_REDIRECTS = 5


def validate_source(source: dict | None, needs_file: bool) -> dict:
    """Validate a Hugging Face source dict from a DEPLOY command. Returns a clean copy."""
    if not isinstance(source, dict) or source.get("type") != "huggingface":
        raise WorkloadError("INVALID_MODEL", "Unsupported model source")
    repo, revision = str(source.get("repo", "")), str(source.get("revision", ""))
    if not REPO_RE.fullmatch(repo) or ".." in repo:
        raise WorkloadError("INVALID_MODEL", "Invalid repository id")
    if not REVISION_RE.fullmatch(revision):
        raise WorkloadError("INVALID_MODEL", "Revision must be a pinned 40-character commit")
    clean = {"type": "huggingface", "repo": repo, "revision": revision}
    if needs_file:
        file, sha = str(source.get("file", "")), str(source.get("sha256", ""))
        if not FILE_RE.fullmatch(file):
            raise WorkloadError("INVALID_MODEL", "Invalid GGUF file name")
        if not SHA256_RE.fullmatch(sha):
            raise WorkloadError("INVALID_MODEL", "Missing or invalid SHA-256")
        try:
            size = int(source.get("size", 0))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            size = 0
        clean.update(file=file, sha256=sha, size=size)
    return clean


def host_allowed(url: str, allowed: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
    parsed = urlparse(url)
    if parsed.scheme != "https" or not parsed.hostname or parsed.username or parsed.password:
        return False
    host = parsed.hostname.lower()
    for pattern in allowed:
        pattern = pattern.lower()
        if pattern.startswith("*."):
            if host.endswith(pattern[1:]):
                return True
        elif host == pattern:
            return True
    return False


class ModelStore:
    def __init__(
        self,
        root: Path,
        allowed_hosts: tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_ALLOWED_HOSTS,
        transport: httpx.AsyncBaseTransport | None = None,
        base_url: str = "https://huggingface.co",
    ):
        self.root = root
        self.allowed = allowed_hosts
        self._transport = transport
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")

    def path_for(self, sha256: str) -> Path:
        return self.root / f"{sha256}.gguf"

    def is_cached(self, source: dict) -> bool:
        path = self.path_for(source["sha256"])
        return path.is_file() and (not source.get("size") or path.stat().st_size == source["size"])

    async def fetch_gguf(self, source: dict, progress: Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]]) -> Path:
        """Download (or reuse) a verified GGUF file. Raises WorkloadError with transient=True for retryable
        network failures."""
        target = self.path_for(source["sha256"])
        if self.is_cached(source):
            return target
        self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
        url = f"{self.base_url}/{source['repo']}/resolve/{source['revision']}/{source['file']}"
        part = target.with_suffix(".part")
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        offset = 0
        if part.exists():  # resume an interrupted download
            with open(part, "rb") as fh:
                for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
                    digest.update(chunk)
            offset = part.stat().st_size
        expected = int(source.get("size") or 0)
        timeout = httpx.Timeout(connect=15.0, read=120.0, write=30.0, pool=15.0)
        try:
            async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout, transport=self._transport, follow_redirects=False) as client:
                resp = await self._open(client, url, offset)
                try:
                    if resp.status_code == 200 and offset:
                        # Server ignored the range request: start over.
                        part.unlink(missing_ok=True)
                        digest, offset = hashlib.sha256(), 0
                    total = expected or (offset + int(resp.headers.get("content-length", 0) or 0))
                    done, last_pct = offset, -10
                    with open(part, "ab") as fh:
                        async for chunk in resp.aiter_bytes(1 << 20):
                            done += len(chunk)
                            if expected and done > expected:
                                raise WorkloadError(
                                    "MODEL_INTEGRITY_FAILED", "Download is larger than the catalog says"
                                )
                            digest.update(chunk)
                            fh.write(chunk)
                            if total:
                                pct = done * 100 // total
                                if pct >= last_pct + 10:
                                    last_pct = pct
                                    await progress(f"Downloading model: {pct}%")
                finally:
                    await resp.aclose()
        except httpx.TimeoutException:
            raise WorkloadError("MODEL_PULL_STALLED", "Model download stalled", transient=True) from None
        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
            raise WorkloadError(
                "MODEL_PULL_FAILED", f"Model download failed: {type(exc).__name__}", transient=True
            ) from None
        if digest.hexdigest() != source["sha256"] or (expected and done != expected):
            part.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            raise WorkloadError("MODEL_INTEGRITY_FAILED", "Downloaded file does not match the catalog's SHA-256")
        os.replace(part, target)
        return target

    async def _open(self, client: httpx.AsyncClient, url: str, offset: int) -> httpx.Response:
        headers = {"Range": f"bytes={offset}-"} if offset else {}
        for _ in range(MAX_REDIRECTS + 1):
            if not host_allowed(url, self.allowed):
                raise WorkloadError("MODEL_SOURCE_REJECTED", f"Refusing to download from {urlparse(url).hostname}")
            request = client.build_request("GET", url, headers=headers)
            resp = await client.send(request, stream=True)
            if resp.status_code in (301, 302, 303, 307, 308):
                location = resp.headers.get("location", "")
                await resp.aclose()
                url = str(httpx.URL(url).join(location))
                continue
            if resp.status_code in (401, 403):
                await resp.aclose()
                raise WorkloadError(
                    "MODEL_ACCESS_DENIED", "Model is gated or private; AgentMesh does not send access tokens to nodes"
                )
            if resp.status_code == 404:
                await resp.aclose()
                raise WorkloadError("MODEL_PULL_FAILED", "Model file not found at the pinned revision")
            if resp.status_code >= 500 or resp.status_code == 429:
                await resp.aclose()
                raise WorkloadError("MODEL_PULL_FAILED", f"Source returned HTTP {resp.status_code}", transient=True)
            if resp.status_code not in (200, 206):
                await resp.aclose()
                raise WorkloadError("MODEL_PULL_FAILED", f"Source returned HTTP {resp.status_code}")
            return resp
        raise WorkloadError("MODEL_SOURCE_REJECTED", "Too many redirects")

"""HTTP helpers for a worker-managed Ollama instance. Never used against the provider's own Ollama."""

import asyncio
import json
import re
import time

import httpx

from .base import ProgressCallback, WorkloadError

_TRANSIENT = re.compile(
    r"\b5\d\d\b|timeout|timed out|connection|reset|EOF|temporar|unavailable|too many requests|429", re.IGNORECASE
)


def is_transient(text: str) -> bool:
    """Registry and network hiccups are retried; "model does not exist" style errors are not."""
    return bool(_TRANSIENT.search(text))


def tag_names(tag: str) -> set[str]:
    return {tag, f"{tag}:latest"} if ":" not in tag else {tag}


ALLOWED_PATHS = frozenset({"/api/chat", "/api/generate", "/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/completions"})


async def wait_api(base_url: str, timeout: float = 60.0, is_alive=None) -> str:
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as client:
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            if is_alive is not None and not await is_alive():
                raise WorkloadError("RUNTIME_START_FAILED", "Runtime process exited during startup")
            try:
                resp = await client.get(f"{base_url}/api/version")
                if resp.status_code == 200:
                    return str(resp.json().get("version", ""))
            except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError):
                pass
            await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    raise WorkloadError("RUNTIME_START_FAILED", "Runtime API did not become available")


async def pull(base_url: str, tag: str, progress: ProgressCallback, stall_timeout: float = 300.0) -> None:
    last_report = 0.0
    last_pct = -10
    timeout = httpx.Timeout(connect=10.0, read=stall_timeout, write=30.0, pool=10.0)
    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout) as client:
            async with client.stream(
                "POST", f"{base_url}/api/pull", json={"model": tag, "name": tag, "stream": True}
            ) as resp:
                if resp.status_code != 200:
                    body = (await resp.aread())[:300].decode(errors="ignore")
                    raise WorkloadError(
                        "MODEL_PULL_FAILED",
                        f"Model download failed ({resp.status_code}): {body}",
                        transient=resp.status_code >= 500 or is_transient(body),
                    )
                async for line in resp.aiter_lines():
                    if not line.strip():
                        continue
                    try:
                        msg = json.loads(line)
                    except ValueError:
                        continue
                    if "error" in msg:
                        err = str(msg["error"])[:300]
                        raise WorkloadError(
                            "MODEL_PULL_FAILED", f"Model download failed: {err}", transient=is_transient(err)
                        )
                    status = str(msg.get("status", ""))
                    total, done = msg.get("total"), msg.get("completed")
                    now = time.monotonic()
                    if total and done is not None:
                        pct = int(done * 100 / total)
                        if pct >= last_pct + 10 or now - last_report > 15:
                            last_pct, last_report = pct, now
                            await progress(f"Downloading model: {pct}%")
                    if status == "success":
                        return
    except httpx.ReadTimeout:
        raise WorkloadError("MODEL_PULL_STALLED", "Model download stalled", transient=True) from None
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise WorkloadError(
            "MODEL_PULL_FAILED", f"Model download failed: {type(exc).__name__}", transient=True
        ) from None
    raise WorkloadError("MODEL_PULL_FAILED", "Model download ended without success")


async def verify_ready(base_url: str, tag: str, num_ctx: int, timeout: float = 300.0) -> str | None:
    """Ready means the model answers a real generation request, not merely that a process is running."""
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout) as client:
        try:
            resp = await client.post(
                f"{base_url}/api/generate",
                json={
                    "model": tag,
                    "prompt": "Reply with OK.",
                    "stream": False,
                    "options": {"num_predict": 2, "num_ctx": num_ctx},
                },
            )
        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
            raise WorkloadError("HEALTHCHECK_FAILED", f"Test generation failed: {type(exc).__name__}") from None
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise WorkloadError(
                "HEALTHCHECK_FAILED", f"Test generation returned HTTP {resp.status_code}: {resp.text[:200]}"
            )
        data = resp.json()
        if not data.get("done"):
            raise WorkloadError("HEALTHCHECK_FAILED", "Test generation did not complete")
        return await model_digest(client, base_url, tag)


async def model_digest(client: httpx.AsyncClient, base_url: str, tag: str) -> str | None:
    resp = await client.get(f"{base_url}/api/tags")
    for m in resp.json().get("models", []):
        if {m.get("name"), m.get("model")} & tag_names(tag):
            digest = str(m.get("digest") or "")
            return digest if digest.replace(":", "").isalnum() else None
    return None


async def health(base_url: str, tag: str) -> bool:
    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as client:
            resp = await client.get(f"{base_url}/api/tags")
            names = {m.get("name") for m in resp.json().get("models", [])} | {
                m.get("model") for m in resp.json().get("models", [])
            }
            return resp.status_code == 200 and bool(names & tag_names(tag))
    except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError):
        return False

"""Ollama backend for the Docker worker: one container per deployment.

Container hardening: memory and CPU limits, PID limit, all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, read-only
root filesystem with a tmpfs /tmp, no host bind mounts (only the AgentMesh-owned model cache volume), and no
Docker socket. GPUs are attached only when the deployment needs one and the provider allowed GPU use.
The serving port is published on loopback only, or the container joins a private network shared with the
worker. Containers this worker did not create (by label) are never touched.

Network egress: when a workload network is configured (the worker runs in a container), that network is
created as ``internal`` (no route out). The container joins the egress network only while it downloads the
model and is disconnected before it serves any request. In loopback mode (worker on the host) Docker cannot
isolate egress this way, and the runtime reports ``egress_restricted=False``.

Containers do not protect the workload from the host administrator; see docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md.
"""

import asyncio

from . import ollama_api
from .base import ProgressCallback, RuntimeCapabilities, WorkloadError, WorkloadHandle, WorkloadRuntime, WorkloadSpec

LABEL = "io.agentmesh.managed"
LABEL_DEPLOYMENT = "io.agentmesh.deployment"


class OllamaDockerRuntime(WorkloadRuntime):
    name = "ollama"
    backend = "docker"
    allowed_paths = ollama_api.ALLOWED_PATHS

    def __init__(
        self,
        image: str,
        models_volume: str = "agentmesh-models",
        network: str = "",
        docker_host: str = "",
        allow_gpu: bool = False,
        client=None,
        egress_network: str = "",
    ):
        self.image = image
        self.models_volume = models_volume
        self.network = network
        self.egress_network = egress_network if network else ""
        self.allow_gpu = allow_gpu
        self._docker_host = docker_host
        self._client = client

    @property
    def client(self):
        if self._client is None:
            import docker

            self._client = docker.DockerClient(base_url=self._docker_host) if self._docker_host else docker.from_env()
        return self._client

    async def _call(self, fn, *args, **kwargs):
        return await asyncio.to_thread(fn, *args, **kwargs)

    async def capabilities(self) -> RuntimeCapabilities:
        try:
            await self._call(self.client.ping)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            return RuntimeCapabilities(
                "ollama", "", "docker", False, False, True, f"Docker unavailable: {type(exc).__name__}"
            )
        version = self.image.rsplit(":", 1)[-1] if ":" in self.image and "@" not in self.image else self.image
        detail = "container limits; egress " + ("restricted after download" if self.egress_restricted else "open")
        return RuntimeCapabilities("ollama", version[:50], "docker", True, self.allow_gpu, True, detail)

    @property
    def egress_restricted(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.network and self.egress_network)

    async def _ensure_networks(self) -> None:
        import docker

        if not self.network:
            return
        try:
            net = await self._call(self.client.networks.get, self.network)
            if self.egress_network and not net.attrs.get("Internal"):
                raise WorkloadError(
                    "RUNTIME_START_FAILED",
                    f"Workload network '{self.network}' must be internal (no egress); recreate it with --internal",
                )
        except docker.errors.NotFound:
            await self._call(
                self.client.networks.create,
                self.network,
                driver="bridge",
                internal=bool(self.egress_network),
                labels={LABEL: "true"},
            )
        if self.egress_network:
            try:
                await self._call(self.client.networks.get, self.egress_network)
            except docker.errors.NotFound:
                await self._call(
                    self.client.networks.create, self.egress_network, driver="bridge", labels={LABEL: "true"}
                )

    async def _ensure_image(self) -> None:
        import docker

        try:
            await self._call(self.client.images.get, self.image)
        except docker.errors.ImageNotFound:
            try:
                await self._call(self.client.images.pull, self.image)
            except docker.errors.APIError as exc:
                raise WorkloadError(
                    "RUNTIME_IMAGE_UNAVAILABLE", f"Could not pull runtime image: {exc.explanation}"
                ) from None

    def _container_name(self, deployment_id: str) -> str:
        return f"agentmesh-wl-{deployment_id}"

    async def start(self, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> WorkloadHandle:
        import docker

        await self._ensure_image()
        await self._ensure_networks()
        name = self._container_name(spec.deployment_id)
        # A leftover container from an interrupted attempt is ours by name and label; replace it.
        await self._remove_by_name(name)
        port = self.internal_port
        kwargs = dict(
            name=name,
            detach=True,
            labels={LABEL: "true", LABEL_DEPLOYMENT: spec.deployment_id},
            mem_limit=f"{spec.ram_mb}m",
            memswap_limit=f"{spec.ram_mb}m",
            nano_cpus=int(spec.cpu_cores * 1e9),
            pids_limit=512,
            cap_drop=["ALL"],
            security_opt=["no-new-privileges:true"],
            restart_policy={"Name": "no"},
            **self._container_config(spec),
        )
        if spec.gpu and self.allow_gpu:
            kwargs["device_requests"] = [docker.types.DeviceRequest(count=-1, capabilities=[["gpu"]])]
        if self.network:
            kwargs["network"] = self.network
        else:
            kwargs["ports"] = {f"{port}/tcp": ("127.0.0.1", None)}
        try:
            container = await self._call(self.client.containers.run, self.image, **kwargs)
        except docker.errors.APIError as exc:
            raise WorkloadError(
                "RUNTIME_START_FAILED", f"Could not start runtime container: {exc.explanation}"
            ) from None

        if self.egress_restricted:
            # Temporary internet access for the model download only (see prepare_model).
            egress = await self._call(self.client.networks.get, self.egress_network)
            await self._call(egress.connect, container)
        if self.network:
            base_url = f"http://{name}:{port}"
        else:
            await self._call(container.reload)
            binding = container.attrs["NetworkSettings"]["Ports"][f"{port}/tcp"][0]
            base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{binding['HostPort']}"
        handle = WorkloadHandle(
            spec.deployment_id, base_url, "docker", {"container_id": container.id, "name": name, "runtime": self.name}
        )

        async def alive():
            return await self.is_alive(handle)

        try:
            await self._wait_started(base_url, alive)
        except WorkloadError:
            await self.remove(handle)
            raise
        return handle

    # --- hooks for other containerised runtimes (see vllm.py) ---------------------------------------------

    internal_port = 11434

    def _container_config(self, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> dict:
        return {
            "environment": {
                "OLLAMA_HOST": "0.0.0.0:11434",
                "OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE": "-1",
                "OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL": "1",
                "OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS": "1",
                "OLLAMA_NOHISTORY": "1",
            },
            "volumes": {self.models_volume: {"bind": "/root/.ollama", "mode": "rw"}},
            "read_only": True,
            "tmpfs": {"/tmp": "rw,noexec,nosuid,size=512m"},
        }

    async def _wait_started(self, base_url: str, alive) -> None:
        await ollama_api.wait_api(base_url, timeout=90, is_alive=alive)

    async def prepare_model(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec, progress: ProgressCallback) -> None:
        try:
            await ollama_api.pull(handle.base_url, spec.model_tag, progress)
        finally:
            if self.egress_restricted:
                await self._cut_egress(handle)

    async def _cut_egress(self, handle: WorkloadHandle) -> None:
        import docker

        container = await self._get_owned(handle.ref.get("container_id") or handle.ref.get("name", ""))
        if container is None:
            return
        egress = await self._call(self.client.networks.get, self.egress_network)
        try:
            await self._call(egress.disconnect, container, force=True)
        except docker.errors.APIError as exc:
            # Never serve with internet access that was promised to be removed.
            raise WorkloadError("RUNTIME_START_FAILED", f"Could not remove egress access: {exc.explanation}") from None

    async def verify_ready(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> str | None:
        return await ollama_api.verify_ready(handle.base_url, spec.model_tag, spec.num_ctx)

    async def health(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> bool:
        return await self.is_alive(handle) and await ollama_api.health(handle.base_url, spec.model_tag)

    async def _get_owned(self, ref: str):
        import docker

        try:
            container = await self._call(self.client.containers.get, ref)
        except docker.errors.NotFound:
            return None
        if container.labels.get(LABEL) != "true":
            return None  # never touch containers AgentMesh did not create
        return container

    async def is_alive(self, handle: WorkloadHandle) -> bool:
        container = await self._get_owned(handle.ref.get("container_id") or handle.ref.get("name", ""))
        if container is None:
            return False
        await self._call(container.reload)
        return container.status == "running"

    async def _remove_by_name(self, name: str) -> None:
        container = await self._get_owned(name)
        if container is not None:
            await self._call(container.remove, force=True)

    async def remove(self, handle: WorkloadHandle) -> None:
        import docker

        container = await self._get_owned(handle.ref.get("container_id") or handle.ref.get("name", ""))
        if container is None:
            return
        try:
            await self._call(container.stop, timeout=10)
        except docker.errors.APIError:
            pass
        try:
            await self._call(container.remove, force=True)
        except docker.errors.NotFound:
            pass

"""Ollama backend for the installable agent: one dedicated ``ollama serve`` process per deployment.

Isolation from the provider's own setup: a random loopback port, a separate model directory under the
worker's data dir, and a minimal environment. The provider's existing Ollama service, port 11434, and
~/.ollama are never used. When systemd user scopes are available, each process runs in its own cgroup with
MemoryMax and CPUQuota; otherwise limits are advisory (scheduler reservations only) and that is reported.

This backend is not a security sandbox: the runtime runs as the provider's user.
"""

import asyncio
import os
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

from . import ollama_api
from .base import ProgressCallback, RuntimeCapabilities, WorkloadError, WorkloadHandle, WorkloadRuntime, WorkloadSpec
from .process_utils import CgroupProbe, base_env, free_port, own_process, spawn, terminate

_free_port = free_port  # kept for callers that imported the old private name


class OllamaProcessRuntime(WorkloadRuntime):
    name = "ollama"
    backend = "process"
    allowed_paths = ollama_api.ALLOWED_PATHS

    def __init__(self, data_dir: Path, binary: str = "ollama", cgroup_limits: bool = True):
        self.data_dir = data_dir
        self.models_dir = data_dir / "models"
        self.logs_dir = data_dir / "logs"
        self.binary = shutil.which(binary) or binary
        self.cgroups = CgroupProbe(cgroup_limits)
        self._procs: dict[str, asyncio.subprocess.Process] = {}

    async def _cgroups_available(self) -> bool:
        return await self.cgroups.available()

    async def capabilities(self) -> RuntimeCapabilities:
        version, available, detail = "", False, ""
        if os.path.isfile(self.binary) and os.access(self.binary, os.X_OK):
            proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
                self.binary, "--version", stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT
            )
            out, _ = await proc.communicate()
            version = next((tok for tok in out.decode(errors="ignore").split() if tok[:1].isdigit()), "")[:50]
            available = True
        else:
            detail = "ollama binary not found"
        cg = await self._cgroups_available()
        return RuntimeCapabilities(
            name="ollama",
            version=version,
            backend="process",
            available=available,
            gpu=False,
            limits_enforced=cg,
            detail=detail or ("cgroup limits via systemd user scope" if cg else "limits advisory"),
        )

    def _env(self, port: int, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> dict[str, str]:
        env = base_env(self.data_dir / "home", spec.gpu)
        env.update(
            {
                "OLLAMA_HOST": f"127.0.0.1:{port}",
                "OLLAMA_MODELS": str(self.models_dir),
                "OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE": "-1",
                "OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL": "1",
                "OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS": "1",
                "OLLAMA_NOHISTORY": "1",
            }
        )
        return env

    async def start(self, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> WorkloadHandle:
        for d in (self.models_dir, self.logs_dir, self.data_dir / "home"):
            d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
        port = free_port()
        cgroup = await self._cgroups_available()
        proc = await spawn(
            [self.binary, "serve"],
            env=self._env(port, spec),
            log_path=self.logs_dir / f"{spec.deployment_id}.log",
            scope=f"agentmesh-wl-{spec.deployment_id[:8]}-{port}" if cgroup else None,
            ram_mb=spec.ram_mb,
            cpu_cores=spec.cpu_cores,
        )
        self._procs[spec.deployment_id] = proc
        handle = WorkloadHandle(
            deployment_id=spec.deployment_id,
            base_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}",
            backend="process",
            ref={"pid": proc.pid, "port": port, "cgroup": cgroup, "runtime": self.name},
        )

        async def alive():
            return proc.returncode is None

        try:
            await ollama_api.wait_api(handle.base_url, timeout=60, is_alive=alive)
        except WorkloadError:
            await self.remove(handle)
            raise
        return handle

    async def prepare_model(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec, progress: ProgressCallback) -> None:
        await ollama_api.pull(handle.base_url, spec.model_tag, progress)

    async def verify_ready(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> str | None:
        return await ollama_api.verify_ready(handle.base_url, spec.model_tag, spec.num_ctx)

    async def health(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> bool:
        return await self.is_alive(handle) and await ollama_api.health(handle.base_url, spec.model_tag)

    def _own_process(self, handle: WorkloadHandle):
        # Ollama receives its port through OLLAMA_HOST (environment), not its command line.
        return own_process(handle.ref.get("pid"), "ollama", handle.ref.get("port"))

    async def is_alive(self, handle: WorkloadHandle) -> bool:
        return self._own_process(handle) is not None

    async def remove(self, handle: WorkloadHandle) -> None:
        await terminate(self._own_process(handle), self._procs.pop(handle.deployment_id, None))

LANGUAGE: python   LINES: 141

"""Launching and supervising runtime processes for the installable agent (shared by all process runtimes).

Each runtime instance runs as the provider's user on a random loopback port, in its own process group, and -
when systemd user scopes are available - in its own cgroup with MemoryMax, MemorySwapMax=0 and CPUQuota.
Only a minimal environment is passed. Processes are identified by PID *and* command line, so a reused PID is
never mistaken for one of ours.
"""

import asyncio
import contextlib
import os
import shutil
import signal
import socket
from pathlib import Path

import psutil

from .base import WorkloadError


def free_port() -> int:
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        return int(s.getsockname()[1])


class CgroupProbe:
    """Detects (once) whether `systemd-run --user --scope` works on this machine."""

    def __init__(self, wanted: bool):
        self.wanted = wanted
        self._available: bool | None = None

    async def available(self) -> bool:
        if self._available is None:
            self._available = False
            if self.wanted and shutil.which("systemd-run"):
                proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
                    "systemd-run",
                    "--user",
                    "--scope",
                    "--quiet",
                    "-p",
                    "MemoryMax=64M",
                    "true",
                    stdout=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
                    stderr=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
                )
                self._available = (await proc.wait()) == 0
        return self._available


def base_env(home: Path, gpu: bool) -> dict[str, str]:
    env = {"PATH": os.environ.get("PATH", "/usr/bin:/bin"), "HOME": str(home)}
    # systemd-run needs these to reach the user service manager; nothing else from the provider's env leaks.
    for key in ("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR", "DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS"):
        if key in os.environ:
            env[key] = os.environ[key]
    if not gpu:
        env.update({"CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "-1", "HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "-1", "ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "-1"})
    return env


async def spawn(
    argv: list[str], *, env: dict[str, str], log_path: Path, scope: str | None, ram_mb: int, cpu_cores: int
) -> asyncio.subprocess.Process:
    """Start ``argv`` in a new session, optionally wrapped in a limited systemd user scope."""
    if scope:
        argv = [
            "systemd-run",
            "--user",
            "--scope",
            "--quiet",
            f"--unit={scope}",
            "-p",
            f"MemoryMax={ram_mb}M",
            "-p",
            "MemorySwapMax=0",
            "-p",
            f"CPUQuota={cpu_cores * 100}%",
            "--",
            *argv,
        ]
    log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
    log = open(log_path, "ab")  # noqa: SIM115
    try:
        return await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            *argv, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=log, stdin=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True
        )
    except OSError as exc:
        raise WorkloadError("RUNTIME_START_FAILED", f"Could not start {Path(argv[0]).name}: {exc.strerror}") from None
    finally:
        log.close()


def own_process(pid: int | None, marker: str, port: int | None) -> psutil.Process | None:
    """Return the process only if it is still the runtime we started: same PID, a command line containing
    ``marker`` and (when known) the port we assigned. Guards against PID reuse."""
    if not pid:
        return None
    try:
        p = psutil.Process(pid)
        cmd = " ".join(p.cmdline())
        if marker not in cmd:
            return None
        if port is not None and str(port) not in cmd:
            with contextlib.suppress(psutil.Error):
                if not any(str(port) in v for v in p.environ().values()):
                    return None
        return p
    except psutil.Error:
        return None


async def terminate(p: psutil.Process | None, proc: asyncio.subprocess.Process | None) -> None:
    """SIGTERM the process group, wait, then SIGKILL. Reaps through asyncio when we own the Process object."""
    if p is None:
        return
    with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):
        os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
    if await _wait_gone(p, proc, 15):
        return
    with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):
        os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
    await _wait_gone(p, proc, 5)


async def _wait_gone(p: psutil.Process, proc, timeout: float) -> bool:
    if proc is not None:
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(proc.wait(), timeout)
            return True
        except TimeoutError:
            return False
    deadline = asyncio.get_running_loop().time() + timeout
    while asyncio.get_running_loop().time() < deadline:
        if not p.is_running() or p.status() == psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE:
            return True
        await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
    return False

"""vLLM backends (GPU only): a ``vllm serve`` process (installable agent) or a vllm/vllm-openai container
(Docker worker).

Differences from Ollama and llama.cpp:

* GPU required. Non-GPU deployments are refused rather than run slowly or not at all.
* vLLM downloads the full Hugging Face repository itself at the pinned commit. Integrity rests on the pinned
  revision (content-addressed by the Hub); there is no single-file SHA-256 as with GGUF.
* Only the OpenAI-compatible routes are exposed. Readiness: /health 200, then a real test generation.
* vLLM's usage telemetry is disabled.

STATUS: implemented and unit-tested with fakes only. It has not run on real GPU hardware (see
docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md).
"""

import asyncio
import os
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

from .base import ProgressCallback, RuntimeCapabilities, WorkloadError, WorkloadHandle, WorkloadRuntime, WorkloadSpec
from .model_store import validate_source
from .ollama_docker import OllamaDockerRuntime
from .process_utils import CgroupProbe, base_env, free_port, own_process, spawn, terminate

LOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1800  # includes downloading the weights
NO_TELEMETRY = {"VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS": "1", "DO_NOT_TRACK": "1", "HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY": "1"}


def _check_spec(spec: WorkloadSpec) -> dict:
    if not spec.gpu:
        raise WorkloadError("UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME", "vLLM deployments require a GPU")
    return validate_source(spec.source, needs_file=False)


def _serve_args(spec: WorkloadSpec, source: dict, host: str, port: int, gpu_fraction: float) -> list[str]:
    return [
        "--model",
        source["repo"],
        "--revision",
        source["revision"],
        "--host",
        host,
        "--port",
        str(port),
        "--served-model-name",
        spec.model_tag,
        "--max-model-len",
        str(spec.num_ctx),
        "--gpu-memory-utilization",
        f"{gpu_fraction:.2f}",
        "--disable-log-requests",
    ]


async def _wait_ready(base_url: str, alive, timeout: float = LOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) -> None:
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as client:
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            if not await alive():
                raise WorkloadError("RUNTIME_START_FAILED", "vLLM exited while loading the model")
            try:
                if (await client.get(f"{base_url}/health")).status_code == 200:
                    return
            except httpx.HTTPError:
                pass
            await asyncio.sleep(2)
    raise WorkloadError("MODEL_PULL_STALLED", "vLLM did not finish loading the model in time", transient=True)


async def _test_generation(base_url: str, spec: WorkloadSpec, source: dict) -> str:
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120.0) as client:
        try:
            resp = await client.post(
                f"{base_url}/v1/chat/completions",
                json={
                    "model": spec.model_tag,
                    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK."}],
                    "max_tokens": 2,
                },
            )
        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
            raise WorkloadError("HEALTHCHECK_FAILED", f"Test generation failed: {type(exc).__name__}") from None
    if resp.status_code != 200 or not resp.json().get("choices"):
        raise WorkloadError("HEALTHCHECK_FAILED", f"Test generation returned HTTP {resp.status_code}")
    return f"hf:{source['revision']}"


def _gpu_fraction(spec: WorkloadSpec, total_vram_mb: int) -> float:
    """Limit vLLM to the VRAM AgentMesh reserved instead of its default 90% of the card."""
    if total_vram_mb <= 0 or spec.vram_mb <= 0:
        return 0.9
    return max(0.1, min(0.95, spec.vram_mb / total_vram_mb))


class VLLMProcessRuntime(WorkloadRuntime):
    name = "vllm"
    backend = "process"

    def __init__(self, data_dir: Path, binary: str = "vllm", cgroup_limits: bool = True, total_vram_mb: int = 0):
        self.data_dir = data_dir
        self.binary = shutil.which(binary) or binary
        self.cgroups = CgroupProbe(cgroup_limits)
        self.total_vram_mb = total_vram_mb
        self._procs: dict[str, asyncio.subprocess.Process] = {}

    async def capabilities(self) -> RuntimeCapabilities:
        available = os.path.isfile(self.binary) and os.access(self.binary, os.X_OK) and self.total_vram_mb > 0
        detail = "" if available else ("no GPU detected" if self.total_vram_mb <= 0 else "vllm not installed")
        return RuntimeCapabilities(self.name, "", "process", available, True, await self.cgroups.available(), detail)

    async def start(self, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> WorkloadHandle:
        _check_spec(spec)
        port = free_port()
        return WorkloadHandle(
            spec.deployment_id, f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}", "process", {"port": port, "runtime": self.name}
        )

    async def prepare_model(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec, progress: ProgressCallback) -> None:
        source = _check_spec(spec)
        port = handle.ref["port"]
        env = base_env(self.data_dir / "home", gpu=True)
        env.update(NO_TELEMETRY | {"HF_HOME": str(self.data_dir / "hf")})
        cgroup = await self.cgroups.available()
        await progress("Starting vLLM (downloads the model at the pinned revision)")
        proc = await spawn(
            [
                self.binary,
                "serve",
                *_serve_args(spec, source, "127.0.0.1", port, _gpu_fraction(spec, self.total_vram_mb)),
            ],
            env=env,
            log_path=self.data_dir / "logs" / f"{spec.deployment_id}.log",
            scope=f"agentmesh-wl-{spec.deployment_id[:8]}-{port}" if cgroup else None,
            ram_mb=spec.ram_mb,
            cpu_cores=spec.cpu_cores,
        )
        self._procs[spec.deployment_id] = proc
        handle.ref.update({"pid": proc.pid, "cgroup": cgroup})

        async def alive():
            return proc.returncode is None

        await _wait_ready(handle.base_url, alive)

    async def verify_ready(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> str | None:
        return await _test_generation(handle.base_url, spec, _check_spec(spec))

    async def health(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> bool:
        if not await self.is_alive(handle):
            return False
        try:
            async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as client:
                return (await client.get(f"{handle.base_url}/health")).status_code == 200
        except httpx.HTTPError:
            return False

    def _own_process(self, handle: WorkloadHandle):
        return own_process(handle.ref.get("pid"), "vllm", handle.ref.get("port"))

    async def is_alive(self, handle: WorkloadHandle) -> bool:
        return self._own_process(handle) is not None

    async def remove(self, handle: WorkloadHandle) -> None:
        await terminate(self._own_process(handle), self._procs.pop(handle.deployment_id, None))


class VLLMDockerRuntime(OllamaDockerRuntime):
    """vllm/vllm-openai container with the same hardening, labels, networks and egress handling as the Ollama
    container. The model is loaded at container start, so readiness is awaited in prepare_model."""

    name = "vllm"
    internal_port = 8000
    allowed_paths = WorkloadRuntime.allowed_paths

    def __init__(self, image: str, hf_cache_volume: str = "agentmesh-hf-cache", total_vram_mb: int = 0, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(image=image, **kwargs)
        self.hf_cache_volume = hf_cache_volume
        self.total_vram_mb = total_vram_mb

    async def capabilities(self) -> RuntimeCapabilities:
        caps = await super().capabilities()
        caps.name = self.name
        caps.gpu = True
        if not (self.allow_gpu and self.total_vram_mb > 0):
            caps.available, caps.detail = False, "vLLM needs a GPU and AGENTMESH_ALLOW_GPU=true"
        return caps

    def _container_config(self, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> dict:
        source = _check_spec(spec)
        return {
            "command": _serve_args(
                spec, source, "0.0.0.0", self.internal_port, _gpu_fraction(spec, self.total_vram_mb)
            ),
            "environment": NO_TELEMETRY | {"HF_HOME": "/cache/hf"},
            "volumes": {self.hf_cache_volume: {"bind": "/cache/hf", "mode": "rw"}},
            # vLLM writes compile caches under $HOME; keep the root filesystem writable but give it shared memory
            # for tensor-parallel workers instead of using the host IPC namespace.
            "read_only": False,
            "shm_size": "2g",
            "tmpfs": {"/tmp": "rw,nosuid,size=2g"},
        }

    async def start(self, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> WorkloadHandle:
        _check_spec(spec)
        if not self.allow_gpu:
            raise WorkloadError("UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME", "GPU use is not allowed on this node")
        return await super().start(spec)

    async def _wait_started(self, base_url: str, alive) -> None:
        return None  # loading (and downloading) happens in prepare_model

    async def prepare_model(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec, progress: ProgressCallback) -> None:
        await progress("vLLM is downloading and loading the model at the pinned revision")

        async def alive():
            return await self.is_alive(handle)

        try:
            await _wait_ready(handle.base_url, alive)
        finally:
            if self.egress_restricted:
                await self._cut_egress(handle)

    async def verify_ready(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> str | None:
        return await _test_generation(handle.base_url, spec, _check_spec(spec))

    async def health(self, handle: WorkloadHandle, spec: WorkloadSpec) -> bool:
        if not await self.is_alive(handle):
            return False
        try:
            async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as client:
                return (await client.get(f"{handle.base_url}/health")).status_code == 200
        except httpx.HTTPError:
            return False

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Back up the AgentMesh PostgreSQL database to a compressed, timestamped custom-format dump.
#
#   DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@host:5432/agentmesh ops/backup_db.sh /var/backups/agentmesh
#
# Keeps the newest $KEEP dumps (default 14) in the target directory. Set PG_DUMP to use a specific binary
# (it must be at least the server's major version), e.g. PG_DUMP="docker run --rm --network host postgres:16 pg_dump".
set -euo pipefail

dest="${1:?usage: backup_db.sh <directory>}"
url="${DATABASE_URL:?DATABASE_URL is required}"
url="${url/postgresql+asyncpg:/postgresql:}"   # libpq does not know the SQLAlchemy driver suffix
keep="${KEEP:-14}"
pg_dump="${PG_DUMP:-pg_dump}"

mkdir -p "$dest"
umask 077   # dumps contain account and ledger data
file="$dest/agentmesh-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).dump"
$pg_dump --format=custom --no-owner --no-privileges --dbname="$url" > "$file.partial"
mv "$file.partial" "$file"
echo "Wrote $file ($(du -h "$file" | cut -f1))"

ls -1t "$dest"/agentmesh-*.dump 2>/dev/null | tail -n +"$((keep + 1))" | xargs -r rm -f

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Restore a dump made by backup_db.sh into an EMPTY database, then report the schema revision.
#
#   DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@host:5432/agentmesh_restore ops/restore_db.sh agentmesh-....dump
#
# Restore into a new database and point the API at it after checking it; never restore over a live one.
# Afterwards run `alembic upgrade head` if the dump predates the deployed code, then
# GET /api/v1/admin/reconciliation to confirm the ledger is consistent.
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:?usage: restore_db.sh <dump file>}"
url="${DATABASE_URL:?DATABASE_URL is required}"
url="${url/postgresql+asyncpg:/postgresql:}"
pg_restore="${PG_RESTORE:-pg_restore}"
psql="${PSQL:-psql}"

tables=$($psql "$url" -tAc "select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'")
if [ "$tables" != "0" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to restore: the target database is not empty ($tables tables)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
$pg_restore --no-owner --no-privileges --exit-on-error --dbname="$url" < "$file"
echo "Restored $file; schema revision: $($psql "$url" -tAc 'select version_num from alembic_version')"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# AgentMesh worker installer (Linux and macOS). Installs for the current user only; never needs root.
#
#   ./install.sh --control-plane https://agentmesh.example.com --token am_enroll_... \
#       [--max-ram-mb 8192] [--max-cpu 4] [--max-disk-mb 30000] [--schedule "mon-fri 18:00-08:00"] \
#       [--outside-schedule pause|drain] [--wheel path/to/agentmesh_worker-*.whl] [--name agentmesh-worker] \
#       [--prefix ~/.local/share/agentmesh] [--update-public-key KEY] [--no-service] [--linger] [--yes]
#
# What it does: checks prerequisites, creates a private Python environment under --prefix, writes
# ~/.config/agentmesh/<name>.env (0600), enrolls this machine with the one-time token, and installs a
# per-user background service. It does NOT install, configure, or touch Ollama, and does not change system
# settings. Remove everything with uninstall.sh.
set -euo pipefail

CONTROL_PLANE="" TOKEN="" WHEEL="" NAME="agentmesh-worker" PREFIX="${HOME}/.local/share/agentmesh"
MAX_CPU="" MAX_RAM="" MAX_DISK="" SCHEDULE="" OUTSIDE="pause" OLLAMA_BIN="" UPDATE_KEY=""
SERVICE=1 LINGER="" ASSUME_YES=0 INSECURE="false"

die() { echo "error: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "==> $*"; }

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --control-plane) CONTROL_PLANE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --token) TOKEN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --wheel) WHEEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --name) NAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --prefix) PREFIX="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --max-cpu) MAX_CPU="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --max-ram-mb) MAX_RAM="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --max-disk-mb) MAX_DISK="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --schedule) SCHEDULE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --outside-schedule) OUTSIDE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ollama) OLLAMA_BIN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --update-public-key) UPDATE_KEY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --allow-insecure-http) INSECURE="true"; shift ;;
    --no-service) SERVICE=0; shift ;;
    --linger) LINGER="--linger"; shift ;;
    --yes|-y) ASSUME_YES=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,15p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "unknown option $1 (see --help)" ;;
  esac
done

[[ "$(id -u)" != "0" ]] || die "do not run as root; the worker installs for your user"
[[ -n "$CONTROL_PLANE" ]] || die "--control-plane is required"
[[ "$NAME" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ ]] || die "--name may only contain letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'"
case "$(uname -s)" in Linux|Darwin) ;; *) die "unsupported OS $(uname -s); use the Docker worker" ;; esac

PY="${PYTHON:-python3}"
command -v "$PY" >/dev/null || die "python3 not found (3.11+ required)"
"$PY" -c 'import sys; sys.exit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3, 11) else 1)' \
  || die "Python 3.11+ required, found $("$PY" -V 2>&1)"
"$PY" -c 'import venv' 2>/dev/null || die "python3 venv module missing (Debian/Ubuntu: apt install python3-venv)"

if [[ -z "$OLLAMA_BIN" ]]; then OLLAMA_BIN="$(command -v ollama || true)"; fi
[[ -n "$OLLAMA_BIN" && -x "$OLLAMA_BIN" ]] || die "Ollama not found. Install it from https://ollama.com/download first.
AgentMesh never installs or modifies Ollama; it runs its own isolated instances using your installed binary."

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
if [[ -z "$WHEEL" ]]; then
  WHEEL="$(ls -t "$HERE"/../dist/agentmesh_worker-*.whl "$HERE"/agentmesh_worker-*.whl 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)"
fi
[[ -n "$WHEEL" && -f "$WHEEL" ]] || die "worker wheel not found; pass --wheel or run scripts/build_worker_wheel.py"

CONFIG_DIR="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/agentmesh"
CONFIG="$CONFIG_DIR/$NAME.env"
DATA_DIR="$PREFIX/$NAME"
VENV="$PREFIX/venv-$NAME"

say "Installing AgentMesh worker '$NAME'"
echo "    control plane: $CONTROL_PLANE"
echo "    environment:   $VENV"
echo "    config:        $CONFIG"
echo "    data:          $DATA_DIR"
echo "    ollama:        $OLLAMA_BIN (used read-only; your own Ollama service is not touched)"
if [[ $ASSUME_YES -eq 0 && -t 0 ]]; then
  read -r -p "Continue? [y/N] " answer; [[ "$answer" =~ ^[Yy] ]] || die "aborted"
fi

[[ ! -e "$CONFIG" ]] || die "$CONFIG already exists; run uninstall.sh --name $NAME first"

say "Creating Python environment"
mkdir -p "$PREFIX" && chmod 700 "$PREFIX"
"$PY" -m venv "$VENV"
"$VENV/bin/pip" install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check "$WHEEL"

say "Writing configuration"

  echo "# AgentMesh worker '$NAME' - written by install.sh. Edit, then: agentmesh-worker service install --name $NAME"
  echo "AGENTMESH_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=$CONTROL_PLANE"

  echo "AGENTMESH_MODE=agent"
  echo "AGENTMESH_NODE_NAME=$NAME"
  echo "AGENTMESH_DATA_DIR=$DATA_DIR"
  echo "AGENTMESH_OLLAMA_BINARY=$OLLAMA_BIN"
  [[ -n "$MAX_CPU" ]] && echo "AGENTMESH_MAX_CPU_CORES=$MAX_CPU"
  [[ -n "$MAX_RAM" ]] && echo "AGENTMESH_MAX_RAM_MB=$MAX_RAM"
  [[ -n "$MAX_DISK" ]] && echo "AGENTMESH_MAX_DISK_MB=$MAX_DISK"
  [[ -n "$SCHEDULE" ]] && echo "AGENTMESH_AVAILABILITY_SCHEDULE=\"$SCHEDULE\""
  echo "AGENTMESH_OUTSIDE_SCHEDULE=$OUTSIDE"
  [[ -n "$UPDATE_KEY" ]] && echo "AGENTMESH_UPDATE_PUBLIC_KEY=$UPDATE_KEY"

# Keep the installed wheel so a failed signed update can roll back to it.
mkdir -p "$DATA_DIR/releases" && chmod 700 "$DATA_DIR"

"$VENV/bin/agentmesh-worker" hardware | sed 's/^/    /'

  [[ -t 0 ]] || die "--token is required when not interactive"
  read -r -s -p "Enrollment token (from the provider dashboard): " TOKEN; echo
fi

"$VENV/bin/agentmesh-worker" enroll --token "$TOKEN"

if [[ $SERVICE -eq 1 ]]; then
  say "Installing background service"
  "$VENV/bin/agentmesh-worker" service install --name "$NAME" $LINGER
fi

echo
say "Done. Useful commands:"
echo "    $VENV/bin/agentmesh-worker status        (with AGENTMESH_CONFIG_FILE=$CONFIG)"
echo "    $VENV/bin/agentmesh-worker doctor"
echo "    $VENV/bin/agentmesh-worker pause | drain | resume"
echo "    $HERE/uninstall.sh --name $NAME"

# Optional drop-in for the system Ollama service on the inference machine (docs: /docs/ai-agent).
#   sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d
#   sudo cp ollama-agentmesh.conf /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/agentmesh.conf
#   sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart ollama
# Review the limits for your machine first; they apply to everything Ollama runs.
[Service]
# Loopback only: Ollama has no authentication and must never be reachable from the network.

# One model, one request at a time, kept loaded between requests.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remove an AgentMesh worker installed by install.sh: stops the service and all managed workloads, deletes
# credentials, configuration, the private Python environment, and (with --purge-models) downloaded models.
# Revoke the node in the provider dashboard as well.
#
#   ./uninstall.sh [--name agentmesh-worker] [--prefix ~/.local/share/agentmesh] [--purge-models] [--yes]
set -euo pipefail

NAME="agentmesh-worker" PREFIX="${HOME}/.local/share/agentmesh" PURGE="" ASSUME_YES=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --name) NAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --prefix) PREFIX="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --purge-models) PURGE="--purge-models"; shift ;;
    --yes|-y) ASSUME_YES=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,7p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown option $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done
[[ "$NAME" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ ]] || { echo "invalid --name" >&2; exit 1; }

CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/agentmesh/$NAME.env"
VENV="$PREFIX/venv-$NAME"
DATA_DIR="$PREFIX/$NAME"

echo "This removes worker '$NAME': service, workloads, credentials, $CONFIG, $VENV${PURGE:+, and models in $DATA_DIR}."
if [[ $ASSUME_YES -eq 0 && -t 0 ]]; then
  read -r -p "Continue? [y/N] " answer; [[ "$answer" =~ ^[Yy] ]] || exit 1
fi

if [[ -x "$VENV/bin/agentmesh-worker" && -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
  AGENTMESH_CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG" "$VENV/bin/agentmesh-worker" uninstall --service "$NAME" $PURGE --remove-config
elif [[ -x "$VENV/bin/agentmesh-worker" ]]; then
  "$VENV/bin/agentmesh-worker" service uninstall --name "$NAME" || true
fi
rm -f "$CONFIG"
rmdir "$(dirname "$CONFIG")" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -rf "$VENV"
if [[ -n "$PURGE" ]]; then rm -rf "$DATA_DIR"; fi
rmdir "$PREFIX" 2>/dev/null || true
echo "Removed. Remember to revoke the node in the provider dashboard."

"""Build the agentmesh-worker wheel from server/node_agent, with no network access and no build backend.

    python scripts/build_worker_wheel.py            # writes dist/agentmesh_worker-<version>-py3-none-any.whl

The wheel contains only the worker package. Its dependencies come from requirements-worker.txt.
"""

import base64
import hashlib
import io
import re
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PKG = ROOT / "node_agent"
DIST_NAME = "agentmesh_worker"


def _version() -> str:
    text = (PKG / "config.py").read_text()
    return re.search(r'WORKER_VERSION = "([^"]+)"', text).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]


def _requirements() -> list[str]:
    lines = (ROOT / "requirements-worker.txt").read_text().splitlines()
    return [ln.strip() for ln in lines if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith("#")]


def _record_line(name: str, data: bytes) -> str:
    digest = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(data).digest()).rstrip(b"=").decode()
    return f"{name},sha256={digest},{len(data)}"


def build(out_dir: Path, version: str | None = None) -> Path:
    """Build the wheel. ``version`` overrides WORKER_VERSION (used to produce test releases)."""
    version = version or _version()
    dist_info = f"{DIST_NAME}-{version}.dist-info"
    files: dict[str, bytes] = {}
    for path in sorted(PKG.rglob("*.py")):
        if "__pycache__" in path.parts:
            continue
        data = path.read_bytes()
        if path.name == "config.py":
            data = re.sub(rb'WORKER_VERSION = "[^"]+"', f'WORKER_VERSION = "{version}"'.encode(), data)
        files[str(Path("node_agent") / path.relative_to(PKG))] = data
    metadata = [
        "Metadata-Version: 2.1",
        "Name: agentmesh-worker",
        f"Version: {version}",
        "Summary: AgentMesh worker: contribute compute to AgentMesh",
        "License: MIT",
        "Requires-Python: >=3.11",
        *[f"Requires-Dist: {r}" for r in _requirements()],
    ]
    files[f"{dist_info}/METADATA"] = ("\n".join(metadata) + "\n").encode()
    files[f"{dist_info}/WHEEL"] = (
        b"Wheel-Version: 1.0\nGenerator: agentmesh-build\nRoot-Is-Purelib: true\nTag: py3-none-any\n"
    )
    files[f"{dist_info}/entry_points.txt"] = b"[console_scripts]\nagentmesh-worker = node_agent.cli:main\n"
    files[f"{dist_info}/top_level.txt"] = b"node_agent\n"
    record = [_record_line(name, data) for name, data in files.items()] + [f"{dist_info}/RECORD,,"]
    files[f"{dist_info}/RECORD"] = ("\n".join(record) + "\n").encode()

    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    wheel = out_dir / f"{DIST_NAME}-{version}-py3-none-any.whl"
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for name, data in files.items():
            info = zipfile.ZipInfo(name, date_time=(2020, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0))  # reproducible
            info.external_attr = 0o644 << 16
            zf.writestr(info, data, zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED)
    wheel.write_bytes(buf.getvalue())
    return wheel


if __name__ == "__main__":
    target = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ROOT / "dist"
    path = build(target, sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None)
    print(path)
    print("sha256", hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest())

[END OF FILE: server/scripts/build_worker_wheel.py]

"""Create (or promote) an operator or admin account. Operators cannot self-register through the API, so the
first one is created here, by someone with access to the server's database configuration.

    DATABASE_URL=... python scripts/create_operator.py ops@example.com            # prompts for a password
    AGENTMESH_OPERATOR_PASSWORD=... python scripts/create_operator.py ops@example.com --role admin

An existing account with that email is promoted (its password is left unchanged unless --reset-password).
The action is recorded in the audit log.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import getpass
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from sqlalchemy import select  # noqa: E402

from app.core.database import session_scope  # noqa: E402
from app.core.security import get_password_hash  # noqa: E402
from app.models.user import User, UserRole  # noqa: E402
from app.services import audit_service  # noqa: E402

MIN_PASSWORD = 12


def read_password(confirm: bool = True) -> str:
    password = os.environ.get("AGENTMESH_OPERATOR_PASSWORD")
    if password is None:
        password = getpass.getpass("Password: ")
        if confirm and getpass.getpass("Repeat password: ") != password:
            raise SystemExit("Passwords do not match")
    if len(password) < MIN_PASSWORD:
        raise SystemExit(f"Operator passwords must be at least {MIN_PASSWORD} characters")
    return password


async def create_operator(email: str, role: str, reset_password: bool, password_reader=read_password) -> str:
    email = email.strip()
    async with session_scope() as db:
        user = (await db.execute(select(User).where(User.email == email))).scalars().first()
        if user is None:
            user = User(email=email, hashed_password=get_password_hash(password_reader()), role=role, is_active=True)
            db.add(user)
            await db.flush()
            outcome = "created"
        else:
            previous = user.role
            user.role = role
            if reset_password:
                user.hashed_password = get_password_hash(password_reader())
            outcome = f"promoted from {previous}"
        audit_service.record(
            db,
            actor_id=None,
            action="user.operator_provisioned",
            resource_type="user",
            resource_id=user.id,
            details={"role": role, "outcome": outcome, "via": "scripts/create_operator.py"},
        )
        await db.commit()
        return outcome


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("email")
    ap.add_argument("--role", choices=[UserRole.operator.value, UserRole.admin.value], default=UserRole.operator.value)
    ap.add_argument("--reset-password", action="store_true", help="Also set a new password for an existing account")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    outcome = asyncio.run(create_operator(args.email, args.role, args.reset_password))
    print(f"{args.email}: {args.role} account {outcome}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

[END OF FILE: server/scripts/create_operator.py]

FILE 344/379: server/scripts/e2e_failover.py
LANGUAGE: python   LINES: 238

"""Failover acceptance test with real workers: a node dies and its deployment moves to another node.

Needs a control plane started with short timeouts so the test finishes quickly, e.g.:

    HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=15 UNHEALTHY_GRACE_SECONDS=20 MONITOR_INTERVAL_SECONDS=3 \\
      uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000
    python scripts/e2e_failover.py --api http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model smollm2:135m

Both workers run on this machine in agent mode with separate data directories (and model caches).
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
import psutil

SERVER_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def check(name: str, ok: bool, detail: str = "") -> None:
    print(f"[{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name}{' - ' + detail if detail else ''}", flush=True)
    if not ok:
        raise SystemExit(f"Step failed: {name}")


def register(api: str, role: str) -> dict:
    email = f"failover-{role}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com"
    r = httpx.post(f"{api}/api/v1/auth/register", json={"email": email, "password": "e2e-password-123", "role": role})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {r.json()['access_token']}"}


def wait_for(fn, timeout: float, interval: float = 1.0):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        value = fn()
        if value:
            return value
        time.sleep(interval)
    return None


class WorkerProc:
    def __init__(self, api: str, provider: dict, name: str, ollama_binary: str):
        self.dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f"agentmesh-failover-{name}-"))
        self.env = {
            **os.environ,
            "AGENTMESH_CONTROL_PLANE_URL": api,
            "AGENTMESH_DATA_DIR": str(self.dir),
            "AGENTMESH_MODE": "agent",
            "AGENTMESH_NODE_NAME": name,
            "AGENTMESH_MAX_CPU_CORES": "2",
            "AGENTMESH_MAX_RAM_MB": "3072",
            "AGENTMESH_MAX_DISK_MB": "4096",
            "AGENTMESH_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS": "3",
        }
        if ollama_binary:
            self.env["AGENTMESH_OLLAMA_BINARY"] = ollama_binary
        token = httpx.post(f"{api}/api/v1/nodes/enrollment-tokens", json={"name": name}, headers=provider).json()[
            "token"
        ]
        subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "node_agent", "enroll", "--token", token],
            cwd=SERVER_DIR,
            env=self.env,
            check=True,
            capture_output=True,
        )
        self.node_id = json.loads((self.dir / "credentials.json").read_text())["node_id"]
        self.log = open(self.dir / "worker.log", "w")  # noqa: SIM115
        self.proc = subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "node_agent", "run"],
            cwd=SERVER_DIR,
            env=self.env,
            stdout=self.log,
            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        )

    def runtime_pids(self) -> list[int]:
        data = json.loads((self.dir / "workloads.json").read_text()) if (self.dir / "workloads.json").exists() else {}
        return [w["handle"]["ref"]["pid"] for w in data.values() if w.get("handle")]

    def kill_hard(self) -> None:
        """Simulate the machine dying: worker and its runtimes vanish without a goodbye."""
        pids = self.runtime_pids()
        self.proc.send_signal(signal.SIGKILL)
        self.proc.wait()
        for pid in pids:
            try:
                os.killpg(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
            except ProcessLookupError:
                pass

    def stop(self) -> int | None:
        if self.proc.poll() is None:
            self.proc.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
            try:
                return self.proc.wait(30)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                self.proc.kill()
        return self.proc.returncode


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--api", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="smollm2:135m")
    ap.add_argument("--ollama-binary", default="")
    ap.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=900)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    api = args.api.rstrip("/")
    binary = str(Path(args.ollama_binary).resolve()) if args.ollama_binary else ""

    provider, customer = register(api, "provider"), register(api, "customer")
    a = WorkerProc(api, provider, "node-a", binary)
    b = None
    try:
        check(
            "node A online",
            bool(
                wait_for(
                    lambda: httpx.get(f"{api}/api/v1/nodes/{a.node_id}", headers=provider).json()["status"] == "ONLINE",
                    30,
                )
            ),
        )
        model = next(m for m in httpx.get(f"{api}/api/v1/models").json() if m.get("model_tag") == args.model)
        dep = httpx.post(f"{api}/api/v1/deployments", json={"model_id": model["id"]}, headers=customer).json()
        check("deployment placed on node A", dep.get("node_id") == a.node_id, dep.get("status", str(dep)))

        def status():
            return httpx.get(f"{api}/api/v1/deployments/{dep['id']}", headers=customer).json()

        ready = wait_for(lambda: (lambda d: d if d["status"] == "READY" else None)(status()), args.timeout, 2)
        check("READY on node A", bool(ready))
        endpoint = ready["endpoint"]
        key = httpx.post(
            f"{api}/api/v1/api-keys", json={"name": "failover", "deployment_id": dep["id"]}, headers=customer
        ).json()["key"]
        auth = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}

        def ask() -> httpx.Response:
            return httpx.post(
                f"{endpoint}/api/generate",
                headers=auth,
                timeout=300,
                json={"prompt": "Say OK.", "stream": False, "options": {"num_predict": 8}},
            )

        first = ask()
        check("inference on node A", first.status_code == 200, repr(first.json().get("response", "")[:40]))

        # Second node joins only now, so the first placement was deterministic.
        b = WorkerProc(api, provider, "node-b", binary)
        check(
            "node B online",
            bool(
                wait_for(
                    lambda: httpx.get(f"{api}/api/v1/nodes/{b.node_id}", headers=provider).json()["status"] == "ONLINE",
                    30,
                )
            ),
        )

        t0 = time.monotonic()
        a.kill_hard()
        check("node A killed (worker and runtime)", a.proc.poll() is not None)
        down = ask()
        check(
            "gateway reports the outage cleanly",
            down.status_code in (503, 502),
            f"{down.status_code} {down.json().get('error', {}).get('code')}",
        )

        moved = wait_for(
            lambda: (lambda d: d if d["node_id"] == b.node_id and d["status"] == "READY" else None)(status()),
            args.timeout,
            2,
        )
        check(
            "deployment moved to node B and is READY again",
            bool(moved),
            f"{time.monotonic() - t0:.0f}s, placements={moved['schedule_attempts'] if moved else '?'}",
        )
        check("same deployment id and endpoint", moved["id"] == dep["id"] and moved["endpoint"] == endpoint)
        again = ask()
        check(
            "same API key works against node B", again.status_code == 200, repr(again.json().get("response", "")[:40])
        )
        events = httpx.get(f"{api}/api/v1/deployments/{dep['id']}/events", headers=customer).json()
        path = [e["to_status"] for e in events if e["to_status"]]
        check(
            "history shows the outage and the move",
            path[path.index("UNHEALTHY") :] == ["UNHEALTHY", "SCHEDULED", "PROVISIONING", "STARTING", "READY"],
            " -> ".join(path),
        )
        old = httpx.get(f"{api}/api/v1/nodes/{a.node_id}", headers=provider).json()
        check("node A offline with no capacity held", old["status"] == "OFFLINE" and old["reserved_ram_mb"] == 0)

        pid_before = b.runtime_pids()
        r = httpx.post(f"{api}/api/v1/deployments/{dep['id']}/restart", headers=customer)
        check("restart accepted", r.status_code == 200, r.text)
        restarted = wait_for(
            lambda: (lambda d: d if d["status"] == "READY" and d["restart_count"] == 1 else None)(status()), 300, 1
        )
        check(
            "READY after restart, new runtime process",
            bool(restarted) and b.runtime_pids() != pid_before,
            f"pid {pid_before} -> {b.runtime_pids()}",
        )
        check("inference after restart", ask().status_code == 200)

        httpx.delete(f"{api}/api/v1/deployments/{dep['id']}", headers=customer)
        released = wait_for(
            lambda: httpx.get(f"{api}/api/v1/nodes/{b.node_id}", headers=provider).json()["reserved_ram_mb"] == 0, 60
        )
        check("cleanup on node B after delete", bool(released) and not b.runtime_pids())
        leftovers = [p for p in pid_before + b.runtime_pids() if psutil.pid_exists(p)]
        check("no runtime processes left behind", not leftovers, str(leftovers))
    finally:
        a.stop()
        if b:
            check("node B shut down gracefully", b.stop() == 0)
    print("\nFailover test passed.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
